newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif., to take over theme park, debt.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif., to take over theme park, debt.

text.p: The California city of Vallejo was expected to take over the Marine World Africa USA theme park on Tuesday and assume about $52 million of its long-term debt, a park spokesman said on Monday.
Jeff Jouett, a spokesman for the park, said the non-profit Marine World Foundation plans to transfer ownership of Marine World facilities, animals and debt to the Marine World Joint Powers Authority.
The city decided to assume control of the park and its debt in part because Marine World Africa USA was short about $2 million owed to noteholders on Nov. 1, city officials said.
As part of the takeover, the city will also assume about $52 million of long-term park debt.
Declining revenues and attendance have hurt the park's financially. Attendance has fallen about 19 percent since 1995, when some 1.6 million visited the park.

City officials said the theme park, the largest private employer in the city, was an essential part of the local economy. The park has 1,300 employees during the summer season and about 500 employees year-round.
The city was expected to take over the park on November 1, but the city council had put off a final vote on the proposal until Tuesday.
